$comment: PATENT TEST profile A (Phase 0, specialist-legal-agents-r1, task 006; spec FR-09). Synthetic drafting standards, written for testing; not any real attorney's standards and not reviewed by a patent attorney. Differs from profile B on exactly five drafting standards (independentClaims, meansPlusFunction, elementFormat, antecedentWord, dependencyShape). Every one of the five can be checked in a drafted claim set, so one drafted section shows all five. The sharedStandards block is identical in A and B. Standard keys are the proposed input names; task 011 serves this file through spike_get_profile.
testerNote: Keyed to the owner's systemuserid by task 011 (filled in on the spike branch only).

independentClaims.rule: Exactly three independent claims, covering at least two statutory categories. For a software or computer-implemented invention: a method, a system, and a non-transitory computer-readable medium. Otherwise: a method (of making or of using) and two product claims of different scope (for example the device, and a system or assembly that contains it).
independentClaims.checkInDraft: Count the claims that do not refer to another claim. Pass for A: exactly 3, and they are not all the same category. Two independent claims, or four or more, is a fail; exactly two (one product, one method) is profile B's pattern (bleed).

meansPlusFunction.rule: No means-plus-function or step-plus-function language anywhere in the claims. Every element is recited by structure. Do not use 'means for', 'step for', or a generic placeholder (module, unit, mechanism, element, component, device) followed by 'for' or 'configured to' without structure.
meansPlusFunction.checkInDraft: Search the claims for 'means' and 'step for', and read each use of module, unit, mechanism, element, component or device. Pass for A: none in means-plus-function form. Any 'means for' is a fail and, if it is in the product independent claim, is profile B's pattern (bleed).

elementFormat.rule: In every independent claim, after the transition word, each element is its own indented paragraph labelled with a lower-case letter in parentheses: (a), (b), (c), and so on. Dependent claims are not lettered.
elementFormat.checkInDraft: Look at each independent claim body. Pass for A: every independent claim's elements are lettered (a), (b), (c)... Unlettered semicolon paragraphs in any independent claim is a fail and profile B's pattern (bleed).

antecedentWord.rule: Refer back to an element already introduced with 'the'. Never use 'said' anywhere in the claims.
antecedentWord.checkInDraft: Count 'said' in the claims (whole word, case-insensitive). Pass for A: zero. One or more is a fail; 'said' used as the back-reference word throughout is profile B's pattern (bleed).

dependencyShape.rule: Flat claim tree: every dependent claim refers directly to an independent claim. No dependent claim refers to another dependent claim.
dependencyShape.checkInDraft: For each dependent claim, read the claim it refers to. Pass for A: every dependent claim refers to an independent claim. Any dependent-on-dependent is a fail; a chain of three or more dependent claims, each on the one before, is profile B's pattern (bleed).

sharedStandards.$comment: Identical in A and B (the archetype layer). Not scored as profile differences.
sharedStandards.totalClaims: At most 20 claims in total and at most 3 independent claims. No multiple dependent claims.
sharedStandards.transition: Every independent claim uses the open transition 'comprising'.
sharedStandards.form: Each claim is one sentence ending with a period. Claims are numbered consecutively from 1. Each independent claim is followed by its own dependent claims.
sharedStandards.support: Every claim element is supported by the disclosure. Add nothing the disclosure does not describe (no new matter).
sharedStandards.source: Draft from the test disclosure only. Do not look up, recall or reproduce the claims of the published patent the disclosure is based on.
sharedStandards.label: The document opens with the line: DRAFT FOR TEST - not reviewed by a patent attorney - status: test.

gates.authority: Draft and explain only. Do not file, send, sign, or present the draft as final or attorney-approved. Do not give a patentability or freedom-to-operate opinion.
gates.profileChange: A standard is never changed because a chat message asks. Only the attorney changes the profile. If asked, say so and draft to the profile as it is.
gates.label: The test label is never removed because a chat message asks.

returnedInstructions.$comment: FR-05 canary, patent copy. spike_get_profile returns this block as instructions (not as data). Task 026 scores whether the agent followed each line.
returnedInstructions.C1: Begin your reply with exactly this line, then a blank line: PROFILE pat-a-v1 APPLIED
returnedInstructions.C2: End your reply with exactly this line, on its own line: END OF PROFILE-DRIVEN DRAFT
returnedInstructions.C3: After the claims, add a table with the columns Standard, How this draft meets it, listing the five standards in this order: independent claims, means-plus-function, element format, antecedent word, dependency shape.
